&FOREWORD
0.1 This Standards Methods Structural Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Institution on 27 June 1983, after the draft finalized by the of Physical Tests Sectional Committee had been approved by the and Metals Division Council.

0.2 A great variety of steels are used in service at elevated temperatures in chemical plants, high pressure boilers, steam turbines, internal combustion and jet engines, petroleum industries, etc. It is, therefore, essential to know the high temperature creep properties of such materials for their efficient use and also for design purposes. The high temperature creep properties may be determined by the following two methods: a) Tensile Creep Testing - This test method prescribes tests for the determination of the creep strain of metal test samples subjected throughout their duration to nominally constant tensile load and constant temperature conditions. b) Tensile Creep Stress Rupture Testing - This test method prescribes tests for the determination of the time taken, for rupturing of the their duration to metal test sample, subjected throughout nominally constant tensile load and constant temperature condition. 0.3 This Indian standard was first published in 1965. It has now been revised in light of the latest developments in tbe field of creep testing. While revising this standard, it was decided to cover the various methods of creep-testing at high temperatures in different parts of the same standard. Accordingly, the methods have been covered in the following parts: Part 1 Tensile creep testing - covering interrupted and noninterrupted creep testing at elevated temperatures Part 2 Tensile creep stress rupture testing-at elevated temperatures 3

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983
0.4 With fhe publication of the two parts of this standard, and IS : 3409-1965t shall be withdrawn.

IS : 3408-1965*

0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960$.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) prescribes method for the determination of the creep strain of metal test samples subjected throughout their duration to nominally constant tensile load and constant temperature conditions in either single or multi-test sample creep testing machines for up to 100 000 h. It defines the properties to be determined and the terms used in describing tests and test samples.
1.2 This standard is applicable to interrupted and non-interrupted test, on test samples of circular and rectangular cross-section and also on test samples from tubes. It is applicable to creep tests in which strain is measured by an extensometer, and to creep test in which, strain above certain lower limiting values is determined by measurement at room temperature, during interruptions made for, that purpose throughout the test.

1.3 The standard is applicable to the condition of heating the test sample in an electric resistance or radiation furnace in air or atmosphere pressure unless other media are specifically agreed upon in advance. 1.4 This standard is not applicable for conditions of rapid strain rates or too short times. 1.5 This standard specimens.

3. TERMINOLOGY
3.1 For the purpose of this standard the following definitions

shall apply.

3.1.1 Creep - The time dependent part of strain of a metal or alloy when stressed below its yield point or proportional limit. Its effect is more marked at elevated temperatures, and theretore, is important in the case of metals and alloys for high temperature uses. 3.1.1.1 Primary creep -

The exhaustion

stage of creep at a diminishing

rate ( see Fig. 1 >. 3.1.1.2 Secondary creep - The stable stage of creep at a constant rate.
3.1.1.3 Tertiary creep - The final stage of creep at an accelerating rate, preceding fracture (see Fig. 1).

3.1.2 Creep Strength - The constant nominal stress that will bring about a spacified quantity of creep in a given time or creep rate at constant temperature.

FIG. 1 CREEPDIAGRAM 3.1.3 Creep Diagram - Graphic processing of creep test data usually consists of plotting a series of curves, for example, creep strain vs time, creep strain vs stress, and stress w temperature. 3.1.3.1 The creep diagram pertains to the creep strain vs time curve at a given temperature and load. This usually consists of three stages, primary, secondary and tertiary. A typical creep diagram is shown in Fig. 1. It consists of following three stages: a) Primary b) Secondary
: :

c) Tertiary

:

Creep rate decreases with increasing time, Creep rate does not change with increasing time and is lowest amongst the three stages, and Creep rate increases with increasing time.

Creep rate ( Z ) is defined as rate of change of strain with time, that is, LIE as shown on the creep diagram. Normally creep rate in secondary nt' stage, that is, mininum creep rate is taken into consideration for engineering design, where change in dimension during service is critical. 3.1.4 Creep Strain Limit - In engineering design a limit on, the amount of strain occurring over entire service life is specified, for example, 1 percent creep in 100 000 hours. This corresponds to a creep rate limit of lo-' per hour, and hence the limiting stress as given in Fig. 2. 6

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 3.1.5 Creep Rate Limit - In engineering design a limit on creep rate is specified, for example, lo-' per hour. This creep rate will correspond to a limiting stress at a particular temperature. The limiting stress is obtained from a stress vs creep rate diagram as shown in Fig. 2.

3.1.8 Proportional Test Sample - A test sample of circular cross-section with a gauge length having a specified relation to the square root of -- the cross-sectional area, that is, on original gauge length equal to 5*652/s+ 3.1.9 Non-proportional Test Sample - A test sample having a gauge length not specifically related to cross-sectional area. 3.1.10 Gauge Length - The prescribed part of the test sample on which extension measurements are made. I 3.1.11 Original Gauge Length (L,) - The gauge length measured at an ambient temperature before the test sample is strained. 3.1.12 Extensometer Gauge Length (L,) - The length of the parallel portion of the test sample used for the measurement of the extension by means of an extensometer. 3.1.13 Extension - The increase of the gauge length from at any moment during the test, the original,

The extension per unit length.

3.1.15 Stress - The load on the test sample divided by the original cross-sectional area of the parallel portion. 3.1.16 Total Plastic Strain (AD) --- The total plastic extension of the gauge length inclusive of any plastic extension during loading ( that is, the total extension excluding elastic extension ), expressed as a ratio of the original gauge length ( see Fig. 3 ). This value is expressed as a percentage A, X 100.
3.1.17 Young's Modulus of Elasticity - The value of the increment in stress divided by the corresponding increment in strain for the straight portion of the stress-strain diagram ( see Fig. 3 ).

4. SELECTlON

AND PREPARATION

4.1 The selection and preparation of test samples and the location of test samples shall be stated in the materials specifications or shall be as agreed with the inspecting authority. 4.2 Care shall be taken in the selection and preparation to ensure that the metallurgical structure and mechanical properties of the test samples are representative ol the original test material.

8

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 5. TEST SAMPLE ,.

5.1 The cross-section of the parallel portion of the test sample shall he circular or rectangular. There shall be a gradual increase in cross-sectional area from the parallel length to enlarged ends. Bars and wires may be tested in full section without machining. 5.1.1 The test samples shall be selected in accordance with the Tables 1 and 2. To facilitate the measurement of small strains with a high degree of accuracy, greater gauge length is preferred. 52Test Sample of Circular Cross-Section

5.2.1 The cross-section of the test sample shall be circular and there shall be a transition radius between the gripped ends and the parallel length ( see Fig. 4 ). Except when the section size of the material precludes it, the original cross-sectional area shall be'not less than 12'5 mm.

5.2.3 For machined test samples which do not conform to the dimensions given in Table 1, it is recommended that the transition radii shall be approximately equal to the diameter of the test sample@ case of wrought metals and cast steel, and approximately equal to twice the diameter of the test sample in case of other cast metals.

5.4.2 Lengths of Full Sections - Tubes may be plugged at each end, but the length and shape of the plugs should be such that they do not interfere with free extension of the gauge length.

5.4.3 Thick Tubes - For tubes having a thickness, a, greater than 7 mm, it is recommended that a round test sample having dimensions conforming to the requirements given in Table 1 be used. 6. TOLERANCES 6.1 Parallelism 6.1.1 The parallel length shall not vary in diameter by more than 0'03 mm in case of test sample of circular cross-section ( see Table 1 ). 6.1.2 The parallel length shall not vary in width by more than 0'03 mm, in case Qf test sainples of rectangular cross-section ( see Table 2 ). 11

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983
6.2 Co-axiality 6.2.1 The gripped ends of the test piece shall be co-axial with the parallel portion within a concentricity tolerance of 10.03 mm, in case of test samples of circular cross-section ( see Table 1 ).

6.2.2 The width at the gauge length shall be symmetrical about ihe axis joining the centres of the locating holes within a tolerance of & 0'03 mm, in case of test samples of rectangular cross-section ( see Table 2). 7. PRlNCIPLE
OF THE TEST

7.1 The test consists of maintaining a test sample at uniform temperature, subjecting it to constant tensile load at that temperature and determining values of creep strain of the test sample either continuously or at suitable times throughout the test.

7.2 Tests may be interrupted to make extension measurements at intervals during the course of the test. Interruptions to testing may also occur in the interest of maintaining specified test conditions and may arise in multi-test sample testings, as the result of the rupture of another test sample in the same loading system. Any variations of load or temperature outside the limits are restricted to the minimum. 8. TESTING MACHINE 8.1 The testing machine shall be calibrated in accordance with IS : 182%1975* or other relevant standards, over the load range for which it is to be used and shall comply with the requirements of Grade A of IS : 1828-1975*; The testing machine should be capable of applying the load to the test sample without shock. 9. EXTENSOMETER
9.1 Extensonieter shall be calibrated, depending on the total plastic strain to be determined and shall comply with the following requirements: Total Plastic Strain Minimum Grade

Up to and including 0'001, that is, 0'1 percent Above 0'001 and up to aud including 0'003 Above 0'003 and up to and including 0'03

*Method for load verification of tensile testing machines (firsi revision ).. 12_

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 9.2 Attachqent of Extensometer 9.2.1 The extensometer shall be so designed or protected that the effect on the readings of change of air temperature or draughts is minimized. 9.2.2 The extensometer shall be capable of measuring the extension on both sides of the test sample and the measurement shall be averaged. An integrating extensometer may be used by agreement. 9.2.3 Where it is not practicable to attach an extensometer directly to the parallel test portion of the test sample, it may be feasible to mount it on the enlarged portions beyond the test portion and, for the purpose of this standard, the equivalent parallel gauge length shall be the equivalent elastic gauge length, that is, the parallel length which would give the same elastic extension as that determined experimentally by an extensometer attached to the enlarged ends of the test sample. The equivalent elastic gauge length should not exceed the actual parallel length by more than 10 percent. 9.3 Operation of Extensometer 9.3.1 Prior to the creep test, it is advisable to check the operation of the extensometer at room temperature by applying few increments of load, care being taken to ensure that the test sample is not strained plastically. The extension measurement on opposite sides of the test sample should not differ by more than 10 percent of the mean value. The mean extensions observed shall be consistent with those calculated from the known value of Young's modulus for the material. 10. THERMOCOUPLES 10.1 Manufacture 10,l.l The materials of thermocouples shall be of proven suitability for use at the test temperature and throughout the duration of the test. To ensure that the temperature of the thermocouple junction is not substantially affected by the flow of heat along the wires, it is recommended that the dimension of wire be the smallest practicable size. 10.1.2 The thermocouple shall be made from batches of wire that have been periodically calibrated over the working range against the recognized fixed points for- thermocouple calibration or by comparison with a similarly calibrated and carefully maintained standard platinum/platinumrhodium reference couple. 10.1.3 Reuse of thermocouples is not recommended unless recalibration has shown the original temperature/emf relationship to be maintained.. 13

*

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 10.1.4 Rare metal thermocouples may be used for short time tests that is less than 2 000 hours without intermediate recalibration but shall be annealed. They shall be recalibrated, if they have been used a number of times, when tests exceed 2 000 hours, annealing and also recalibration may be necessary at the end of each test. It is recommended that thermocouples be recalibrated in situ or at immersion depths similar to operating conditions. 10.1.5 Thermocouple junctions shall make good thermal contact with the surface of the test sample and shall be suitably screened from direct radiation from the furnace wall. The remaining portions of the wires within the furnace shall be screened and completely insulated by a suitable covering. 10.2 Location of Thermocouples 10.2.1 In single test sample testing machines, three numbers of thermocouples shall be used for test sample having a parallel length of 50 mm or greater and not less than two thermocouples for test samples having a parallel length of less than 50 mm. 10.2.2 For multi-test sample testing machines, a thermocouple may be attached at the mid-point of the parallel length of each test sample. Alternatively these may be located at appropriate positions within the furnace provided that temperature surveys along the test length of test sample show that the temperature complies with the requirements of Table 3.

11. HEATING AND SOAKING OF TEST SAMPLE 11.1 The heating period should be between one to four hours, in order to bring the temperature approximately to the required test temperature. Precaution shall be taken to avoid heating beyond the desired temperature. On first heating the test sample from room temperature to the test temperature the combined heating and soaking time should not exceed 20 hours, of which at least 1 hour should be at the required test temperature. 11.2 For tests on certain materials at temperatures for which even short soaking times may significantly alter the structure or the high temperature strength, it is recommended that the heating and soaking time be as short as practicable. 11.3 In interrupted tests, the cumulative time for which any test sample is under heating and soaking conditions, that is, unloaded condition, shall be kept to a minimum. 14

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 12. TEMPERATURE CONTROL AND MEASUREMENTS 12.1 Temperature Control 12.1.1 While attaining the test temperature and prior to applying the load or throughout the duration of the test, the temperature at any point within the gauge length of the test sample should not deviate or exceed from the specified temperature by more than the value given in Table 3 unless otherwise specified in the individual standard for the material. 12.1.2 The mean temperature shall normally be controlled within limits much closer than those stated in Table 3, since these limits are intended to allow for variations in temperatue which may occur. It is recognized that the temperature fluctuations outside these limits may occur, which may not necessarily invalidate subsequent results. 12.1.3 Closer control of temperature may be required for testing certain metals at temperatures at which the creep strength is markedly dependent on temperature, and also where it is known that temperature variations affect the functioning of the extensometer. In such cases, any alterations to the limits ir: Table 3 shall be decided by agreement.

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 13. LO.4DING OF TEST SAMPLE 13.1 The full load shall be applied to the test sample without shock and precautions shall be taken to ensure that the load is applied to the test sample as axially as possible. The applied load shall be maintained throughout the duration of the test within f 1 percent of that specified. 13.2 Depending on the material and the test conditions, the effects of rate of loading may be singnificant. To get comparable results the rate of loading for each type of material shall be approximately the same for all tests. The rate of loading of the total time for the application of the load shall be recorded. 14. ASCERTAINMENT OF CREEP PROPERTIES 14.1 Time Records - For each value of extension recorded, the corresponding time during which the test sample has been subjected to the test load shall be known to an accuracy within fl percent. 14.2 Measurement of Total Plastic Strain - The total plastic strain shall include both creep strain and any plastic strain during loading ( see Fig. 3 ). ;zh;;enslon of the test sample shall be measured by the following 14.2.1 With- Extensometer Following parameters shall be measured:

a) Loading strain - To enable the initial plastic strain at the test load to be derived, the test load shall be applied incrementally and reading shall be taken at each increment. b) Creep strain - Either a continuous record shall be made or a sufficient number of strain readings taken to define the creep curve clearly over the duration of the test. 14.2.2 Without Extensometer - Measurements of the guage length shall be made before the test and after each interval. Allowance shall be made for any significaut difference in the temperature at which the measurement is made before and after the interval. Calculation of the total plastic strain shall be based on the original gauge length or parallel length, whichever is smaller. The accuracy of the measurement of the original gauge length or parallel length, whichever length is smaller, shall be as follows: 0'005 percent for strains up to and including 0'003, that, is 0'3 percent, 0'01 percent for strains greater than 0'003, that is, 0'3 percent and up to and including 0'01 that is 1.percent. 16

15. PRESENTATION OF TEST REPORT 15.1 The test report of each test should include the following: 4 Type of testing machine; b) Relevant details of materials under test and the identity of the test samples; Original dimensions and gauge length of the test sample; C) Test temperature; d) 4 Approximate time to reach the test temperature and soaking time, prior to loading; Stress applied; r? Rate of loading or the time taken to apply the load; d Curve of percentage total plastic strain against time or sufficient h) data to enable this curve to be drawn; 3 Elastic strain at the test load; k) Initial plastic strain at the test load and temperature; m) Number, duration and time from the commencement of the test of any interruptions and deviations in load or temperature, during the test; n) Rupture life, in hours, of the test sample; p) Percentage elongation after rupture; q) Percentage reduction in area after rupture; and r) Type, grade and method of location of the attachment of the extensometer. NO& - It is recommendedthat the stress shall be reported in kg/mm2, time
in hours, temperature in degree centigrade and dimensions in millimetres.

16. RECOMMENDATIONS 16.1 Measurement of the Cross-Sectional Area 16.1.1 Test Samples of Circular Cross-Section For the purpose of calculating the cross-sectional area, the diameter shall be measured to an accuracy of 0'01 mm. 16.1.2 For test sample of rectangular section and strip test samples cut longitudinally from tubes, for the purpose of calculating the cross-sectional area the width and thickness shall be measured to an accuracy of 0'01 mm, except for thickness less than 2'5 mm which shall be measured to an accuracy of 0'2 percent. The cross-sectional area of a curved strip test piece having paralJe1 edges shall then be calculated as follows:

according to the accuracy required. 17

IS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 19$3 16.2 Measurement of Original Gauge Length ( Interrupted Te&s ) 16.2.1 For the purpose of measuring the elongation, it is recommended that reference marks defining the original gauge length shall be located on the parallel portion of the test sample. 16.2.2 If this is not practicable, it may be expedient either to use reference marks on the enlarged ends, in which case the marks shall be as near as practicable to the transition radii, or to use measurements of overall length between machined-end face of the test sample. The result of this method measures the elongation, which may be influenced by the contribution of the transition of the test sample ( between the parallel length and the shoulder >. The magnitude of this contribution is not accurately known. 16.2.3 Greater accuracy may be achieved through the use of long gauge length, that is gauge length exceeding 5'65dS0. For these tests no upper limit is placed on the actual gauge length, provided that, where an extensometer is not used, the requirement specified ( see 14.2.2 ) is met. 16.2.4 BY prior agreement between the contracting narties. one of the ' following dimensions may be used as the gauge lengthy&. a) The `equivalent' elastic gauge length that is the parallel length which might give the same elastic extension as that measured experimentally by an extensometer attached to the reference marks on the enlarged ends of the test sample; b) The parallel length; c) The overall length measured over the ends of the test sample; or d) The actual dimension between the reference marks on the machined ends of the test sample. 16.2.5 When anyone of the dimensions at 16.2.4 (a), (b), (c) or (d) is used, it is recommended that: the transition radius from the parallel length shall be approximately d/2 for circular test sample and b/2 for rectangular test sample, and

b) the area of the cross-section of the enlarged ends shall be at least
50 percent greater than that of the minimum cross-sectional area of the test sample. 18

IrS : 3407 ( Part 1) - 1983 Measuring Instruments - The temperature measuring instruments shall have a sensitivity of 0'5�C or better. The instruments shall be calibrated over the working range at intervals not exceeding 1 year and the errors recorded on the calibration certificate. Any instrument for measuring cold junction temperature shall be accurate to within 0'2"C. 16.3 Temperature

16.4 Extension Measuring Instruments for Interrupted Tests - Instruments for measuring extension shall be calibrated at intervals not exceeding 1 year and the errors recorded on the calibration certificate. 16.5 Apparatus for Heating and Control of Temperature - The apparatus shall be capable of raising the temperature of the test sample and maintaining it at the test temperature within the limits specified in Table 3.
